If TZ has changed since the last call (copy kept at 0x20019530), it frees the old copy, duplicates the new string and parses it: the standard name, the standard offset [+-]hh:mm:ss, an optional DST name and offset, and the ',Mm.w.d[/time]' rules. Rules are stored as tzinfo records, ble_219_0c071AE4 (__tzcalc_limits) computes the year's transitions, and daylight is set when the DST offset differs from the standard one.

returns.description: no return value

ble_219_0c071c50.notes: The lookup at 0x0C07247C is named _setenv_r in another wave's annotation, but its use (name argument, NULL test) matches _getenv_r. The tz state block read in mktime through 0x0C0724B0 is also not the locale object that earlier annotation names.

ble_219_0c071f64.name: _vsnprintf_r
ble_219_0c071f64.summary: Newlib _vsnprintf_r: reentrant bounded vsprintf through a stack string FILE
ble_219_0c071f64.description: Reentrant bounded formatter _vsnprintf_r(reent, buf, size, fmt, ap). It works as vsnprintf (0x0C071570) with the reent record passed explicitly. A negative size sets reent errno to 0x8B and returns -1; otherwise a stack string FILE (flags 0x208) is set up and the vfprintf worker (0x0C0725FC) runs. Results below -1 set errno to 0x8B, and when size is non-zero the output is NUL-terminated.

returns.description: number of characters the full output would take, or -1 on error

ble_219_0c071fbc.name: snprintf
ble_219_0c071fbc.summary: Newlib snprintf: variadic bounded format, forwarded to _vsnprintf_r on the global reent
ble_219_0c071fbc.description: Variadic snprintf(buf, size, fmt, ...). It passes the global reent, buf, size, fmt and the variadic words through to _vsnprintf_r (0x0C071F64), which does the formatting. Callers use it to format into bounded buffers.

params.name: param_4
params.description: first variadic argument word, forwarded unchanged

returns.description: number of characters the full output would take, or -1 on error

ble_219_0c071ffc.name: __assert_func
ble_219_0c071ffc.summary: Newlib __assert_func: print the failed assertion with file and line to stderr, then abort
ble_219_0c071ffc.description: Newlib __assert_func(file, line, function, expr). It prints 'assertion "%s" failed: file "%s", line %d%s%s' to stderr (reent+0xC) through fprintf (0x0C07222C), adding ', function: ' when a function name is given, then calls abort (0x0C073764), which does not return; the loop is a guard. The REENT allocation checks in gmtime, rand and strtok call it with their source file and line.

returns.description: does not return

ble_219_0c071ffc.notes: The four arguments come from the callers; the decompiled signature shows none.

ble_219_0c0720d4.name: __sfmoreglue
ble_219_0c0720d4.summary: Newlib __sfmoreglue: allocate a glue block of n zeroed FILE structures for the FILE pool
ble_219_0c0720d4.description: Newlib __sfmoreglue(reent, n). Allocates 12 + 0x68*n bytes with _malloc_r (0x0C071080): 0x68 is sizeof(__sFILE) and 12 is the glue header. On success it sets the header to next = NULL, niobs = n and iobs = the FILE array after the header, then zeroes the array. Returns the glue block, or NULL if the allocation fails.

params.name: param_2
params.description: number of FILE structures in the block

returns.description: new glue block, or NULL

ble_219_0c072130.name: __sinit
ble_219_0c072130.summary: Newlib __sinit: once-only setup of the FILE pool and stdin, stdout and stderr
ble_219_0c072130.description: Newlib __sinit(reent), run with the sinit lock (0x0C072118) held. It only does its work once, tracked by the flag at reent+0x18. It installs the cleanup hook at reent+0x28 and, for the global reent, sets DAT_200049C4 to 1. It allocates three FILEs with __sfp (0x0C0721A0) for stdin, stdout and stderr (reent+4, +8, +0xC), initialises them with std (0x0C072080) using flags 4, 9 and 0x12 and descriptors 0, 1 and 2, then sets the initialised flag and releases the lock with __retarget_lock_release_recursive.

returns.description: no return value

ble_219_0c0721a0.name: __sfp
ble_219_0c0721a0.summary: Newlib __sfp: find or create a free FILE in the glue pool and mark it in use
ble_219_0c0721a0.description: Newlib __sfp(reent). Under the FILE-pool lock (0x0C072100 and 0x0C07210C) it runs __sinit first if the pool is not initialised. It then walks the glue list headed at 0x200049F4, looking for a FILE whose _flags (short at +0xC) are zero. On a match it sets _flags to 1 and the descriptor to -1 (word 0xFFFF0001), initialises its recursive lock with __retarget_lock_init_recursive (0x0C0724B8), clears its buffer and offset fields and the 8-byte mbstate at +0x5C, and returns it. Without a free slot it adds a glue block with __sfmoreglue (0x0C0720D4) and tries again; if that fails it sets errno to 12 and returns NULL.

returns.description: claimed FILE, or NULL

ble_219_0c07222c.name: fprintf
ble_219_0c07222c.summary: Newlib fprintf: variadic formatted output to a FILE through the reent vfprintf worker
ble_219_0c07222c.description: Variadic fprintf(stream, fmt, ...). It forwards the global reent, the stream, the format and the variadic words to the vfprintf worker _vfprintf_r (0x0C072BFC). In this packet its only caller is __assert_func, which passes stderr and the assertion format.

params.name: param_3
params.description: first variadic argument word, forwarded unchanged

params.name: param_4
params.description: second variadic argument word, forwarded unchanged

returns.description: number of characters written, or a negative value on error
